narrative.overview:
The website is a metro route map in the brand's own colours. Your line is peacock teal, the other person's is marigold, and they meet at an interchange drawn as the brand's two rings, only where both fit. After the interchange the two rails run on side by side, and each rule of the product is a station on that line. The language is Delhi Metro-style wayfinding: graphite sign bands across the top and the close, enamel sign plates lettered in white, thick route lines and white station roundels outlined in graphite, all on a white enamel ground. DMRC's identity (its logo, line colours and signage artwork) is never copied; the system borrows the grammar of wayfinding, not anyone's marks.

Density is that of signage: big condensed bold names, short plates, generous white ground between stations, body text kept to readable measures. Every sign that names a place or a rule is bilingual, Devanagari under the Latin. The world is loud enough to be remembered (bands, plates, two saturated lines) and calm in its motion: the only authored movement is the line drawing itself as you travel down the page.

Rejected (confirmed in the direction contract): the category's swipe-card phone mockup and gradients, and the calm cream page. Pills, gradients and glow are out.
keyCharacteristics: Two line colours with fixed meanings: teal is yours, marigold is theirs.
Graphite sign bands and plates on a white enamel ground.
Anek throughout: semi-condensed bold (wdth 87.5) for signs, normal width for text.
Bilingual signs, Devanagari under the Latin.
Square-cornered plates; the only curves are roundels and the two-ring mark.
One authored motion: the rails draw on scroll.

rules.name: The Two Lines Rule
rules.body: Teal always means you and marigold always means the other person. Never swap them, never add a third line colour, and never use them as decoration detached from that meaning (the button plate and focus ring are marigold because they are the step toward someone else).

rules.name: The Rails Are Not Text Rule
rules.body: Marigold on white is for rails, plates and fills only, never for text on the white ground; marigold text appears only on graphite.

rules.name: The Bilingual Sign Rule
rules.body: Every sign that names a place or a rule carries its Devanagari directly beneath the Latin, as a block, at 0.875em of the sign's size with line-height 1.2, marked `lang="hi"`. This covers station plates, panel headings and the direction sign. The wordmark and the map labels set their Hindi at their own fixed sizes. Running text is English only. Open item: all Hindi copy is pending a native reviewer before the site goes live; it is not approved copy, and new Hindi must be added to `scripts/devanagari-text.txt` so the subset font contains it.

rules.name: The Condensed Means Sign Rule
rules.body: Semi-condensed bold is for things that work as signs (names, headings, plates, buttons). Paragraphs are never condensed.

rules.name: The One Geometry Rule
rules.body: On desktop the map's joined rails and the station rails share one geometry: centred at 12.5% and 14.75% of the right grid column, each 1.6% of it wide, so the line runs unbroken from the first screen to the last stop. Change one and you must change the other (`RouteDiagram.tsx` and `landing.module.css`).

rules.name: The Enamel Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat painted planes. Separation is by colour block, never by shadow.

rules.name: The Sign Plate Rule
rules.body: If it is pressed or read as a sign, it is a rectangle. No pills, no rounded cards.

rules.name: The One Moving Idea Rule
rules.body: The rails draw downward as the visitor scrolls (a `scaleY` 0 to 1 keyframe, linear, on a CSS scroll-driven `view()` timeline, range entry 30% to cover 55%; no script). It runs only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` and `@supports (animation-timeline: view())`; otherwise the line is fully drawn from the start. Only the rails move; every word is visible from first paint. This is the world's only authored motion. The end-of-line video loops longer than 5 seconds, so it carries a rectangular graphite pause plate in its bottom-right corner (marigold when pressed) to satisfy WCAG 2.2.2, and the plate is hidden when reduced motion is requested.

dos: Do keep teal for your line and marigold for theirs, everywhere, including the two-ring mark.
Do set every sign that names a place or a rule bilingual, Devanagari beneath at 0.875em, and route new Hindi through a native reviewer before it ships.
Do make anything pressable a square-cornered plate at least 3rem tall, with the marigold-in-graphite focus ring.
Do put marigold text only on graphite; on white, marigold is a rail or a fill.
Do keep the map rails and station rails on one geometry (12.5% and 14.75% of the column, 1.6% wide) at desktop widths.
Do draw map symbols as inline SVG with real text labels, never as images of words.
Do give anything that moves for more than 5 seconds a pause plate, and draw the finished state when motion is reduced or unsupported.
donts: Don't use pills, rounded cards, gradients, glow or drop shadows.
Don't copy DMRC's logo, line colours or signage artwork; the grammar is borrowed, the marks are our own.
Don't add motion beyond the drawing rails and the pausable end-of-line loop.
Don't condense paragraphs; semi-condensed bold is for signs.
Don't use the shared blue focus colour, the shared radius scale or the staff console's coloured left-border notice inside this world.
Don't show people in imagery; the end-of-line loop is people-free footage.
